tool_input.command: git restore -- . && git status --porcelain && git status -sb

result:
Tracked files are clean against `HEAD` (2699396). Working tree reports no modifications.

What I did and why:

- `git restore -- .` was blocked by a Sentinel rule (`git.discard_changes`) because it would have destroyed the changes irrecoverably. Rather than override the guard, I used its suggested alternative.
- `git stash push` on the three modified files: `README.md`, `python-flask/.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`, `python-flask/.devcontainer/on-create-command.sh` (6 added lines total).

Result:

- Tracked files match the last commit — `git status --porcelain` is empty.
- Untracked files were untouched; `git stash push` with explicit pathspecs only takes tracked modifications. (There happen to be none in this checkout anyway.)
- The discarded content is recoverable at `stash@{0}` if you want it back (`git stash pop`), or run `git stash drop` to delete it for good.
